[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Mishka and Interesting sum** [CF 703D · Mishka and Interesting sum](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/703/D){rating="2100"}

Only the *parity* of each value's count matters: a value is "in" the answer iff its count is even and at least $2$. Adding one more copy of $v$ flips that membership — it toggles whether $v$ is XOR-ed in — and XOR is its own inverse, so the running answer is just "XOR $v$ in again" on every flip. The catch: the flip on a copy depends on whether $v$ already had $\ge 1$ copies, so `add` is $O(1)$ but the whole thing is a **toggle**, exactly the shape that snapshot-and-restore handles cleanly (@sec-mo-a2). We use rollback Mo so the right pointer never retreats and there is no hand-written `remove` to get subtly wrong: within a left-block we add rightward monotonically, snapshot, temporarily add the $\le B$ left fringe, read the XOR, then roll the fringe back.

[Solved in full in @sec-mo-p2-interesting.]{.card-link}

:::
